summary: Add CPU, process, memory, spend, attribution and SLO adapters after disk conditions.

replay.detail: Uses disk condition head/observation reconstruction and direct local restart restoration. No replay of historical condition transitions.

schema.detail: Adds the local hourly authored-claim-byte table on open. Storage version stays 18; no replicated schema or generated client change beyond the disk prerequisite.

rules.detail: Inherits the disk prerequisite's unresolved local quorum-free trim and permanent negative-set/transport contract. No checkpoint fallback. Do not queue before disk payload-retention controls and independent approval. OTel copies, copied notification payloads and unchanged durable message retention remain intact.

compatibility.detail: Adds root declaration metric/process/route/window support. Disk-only daemons refuse these declarations; upgrade all members before publishing CPU or other follow-up declarations. Authored bytes are attribution, not physical growth; no first-user condition on attribution. Uses existing performance/SLO windows without changing Meter::record_request or snapshot.

downtime.detail: Ordinary restart; holds restart and standing breaches restore silently. Evaluator cadence stays 30 seconds, database size remains hourly, spend cache five minutes; native process CPU needs two PID/start-time samples. No new service, collector or load generator. Executable names longer than 15 bytes are rejected; short-lived children between samples are undercounted and the per-PID scan cost remains unmeasured.

manual.detail: Operations reviews/deploys after disk-first is deployed and independently approved. No builder merge or deployment. First-user physical daily growth requires the shared hourly sampler and Operations baseline; existing ops missions stay until real breach/recovery and Operations agreement. Production CPU/SQL evidence remains required and unmeasured; missing native readings and bounded process enumeration remain visible limits. Attribution cache authority and two-day retention are documented separately from the three disk tables.

recovery.detail: Roll forward after these declarations exist: a disk-only daemon cannot evaluate CPU/rest metrics. Stop declarations before returning to disk-only code. Notification idempotency and OTLP retry/cursor behavior follow the disk prerequisite.
